skill.name: apple-design
skill.description: Design and review responsive web interfaces using Apple-inspired motion, gesture, material, typography, accessibility, and interaction principles.
skill.summary: Create fluid, interruptible, and accessible web interactions with practical Apple-inspired design guidance.
skill.author: emilkowalski

security_audit.summary: All 62 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, design terminology, and ordinary prose. SKILL.md contains instructional CSS and JavaScript examples but no shell execution, system or network reconnaissance, prompt injection, credential access, or exfiltration intent. No semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Gesture-driven web interfaces often feel delayed, rigid, or visually inconsistent. This skill provides practical guidance for responsive motion, materials, typography, accessibility, and interaction design.
actual_capabilities: Reviews pointer, drag, swipe, drawer, sheet, and carousel interactions for direct manipulation and immediate feedback.
Recommends spring damping, response, velocity handoff, momentum projection, and interruptible transition patterns.
Explains rubber-banding, gesture thresholds, spatial consistency, anchored origins, and frame-level motion quality.
Guides translucent materials, depth, typography, optical sizing, tracking, leading, and visual hierarchy.
Applies reduced-motion, reduced-transparency, contrast, text scaling, and inclusive interaction considerations.
Uses Apple-inspired design principles to evaluate purpose, agency, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, and delight.
limitations: Provides design guidance and examples, but does not include a runtime package or complete component library.
Offers Apple-inspired web patterns, but does not certify compliance with official Apple platform requirements.
Requires testing on real browsers, devices, input methods, and accessibility settings.
Sample motion values need tuning for each component, layout, animation library, and product context.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Interactions
use_cases.description: Review buttons, sheets, drawers, and gestures for immediate feedback, interruptibility, momentum, and predictable spatial behavior.

use_cases.title: Implement Fluid Web Motion
use_cases.description: Translate interaction specifications into pointer events, spring animations, velocity handoff, rubber-banding, and accessible motion alternatives.

use_cases.title: Audit Interface Quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate motion, materials, typography, hierarchy, accessibility, and interaction consistency before a product release.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this button interaction for immediate feedback and accessibility. Identify latency, unclear states, and specific improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single interactive control

prompt_templates.title: Design a Bottom Sheet
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a mobile bottom sheet with direct dragging, velocity-aware release, snap points, interruption, rubber-banding, and reduced-motion behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Interaction Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interface flow using Apple-inspired principles. Cover feedback, spatial consistency, gesture conflicts, materials, typography, accessibility, and user agency.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Motion System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a web motion system for these components. Define spring families, velocity rules, interruption behavior, gesture thresholds, accessibility alternatives, and validation tests.

output_examples.input: Review a card carousel that snaps only after the finger releases.
output: Add continuous one-to-one tracking during the drag.
Project the resting position from release velocity before choosing a snap point.
Carry release velocity into an interruptible spring and preserve the original grab offset.

output_examples.input: Recommend motion for a dismissible settings sheet.
output_examples.output: Use a responsive spring with limited bounce, symmetric entry and exit paths, source-aware origin, drag interruption, and a reduced-motion cross-fade.

output_examples.input: Audit a translucent toolbar with low-contrast text.
output_examples.output: Increase foreground contrast, avoid stacked translucent layers, strengthen material separation, and provide solid alternatives for reduced transparency and increased contrast.

best_practices: Test interactions with real pointer movement, reversal, interruption, and rapid repeated input.
Tune motion from the current visible state and preserve velocity across gesture-to-animation handoffs.
Validate every motion and material choice with reduced-motion, transparency, contrast, and text-size settings.
anti_patterns: Do not lock input until an animation finishes or restart motion from a stale target value.
Do not add bounce, blur, sound, or haptics without a clear interaction purpose.
Do not treat visual polish as a substitute for predictable navigation, readable text, and user control.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete interface code?
faq.answer: It provides design guidance and focused examples. Complete production components still require implementation, integration, testing, and product-specific decisions.

faq.question: Which interactions benefit most from this guidance?
faq.answer: Drag, swipe, sheet, drawer, carousel, menu, modal, slider, and other gesture-driven interactions benefit most.

faq.question: Does every animation need a spring?
faq.answer: No. Springs suit interruptible physical interactions, while short fades or simple transitions can suit non-gesture state changes.

faq.question: How does the skill address accessibility?
faq.answer: It covers reduced motion, reduced transparency, increased contrast, scalable typography, continuous feedback, and alternatives to vestibular motion.

faq.question: Can I use these principles outside Apple platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance translates interaction and motion principles to web interfaces while respecting browser and device constraints.

faq.question: Are the sample spring values universal?
faq.answer: No. They are starting points that require tuning for component size, travel distance, input velocity, library behavior, and product tone.
